what: unit tests for the O4 instruments sealed in §五. Every check has a negative partner: an instrument that cannot fail is not conservative, it is broken.

results.test: band width is per card, then averaged (3 and 12 -> 7.5)
a smeared profile would read WIDER than either card -- the defect the sealed coding avoids
band energy is continuous where band width ties
true silhouette is exactly the pixels the glass changes
a REAL gutter leak fails
ink INSIDE the silhouette is not counted as gutter invasion
a flat layout quad is NOT the gutter boundary -- the silhouette is derived from rendered pixels, so a bulged lens keeps its own annulus
a ZERO-baseline saturation change takes the ABSOLUTE branch
results.detail: {"coding": "absolute", "codingChosenBy": "baseline interior saturation 0.00000 < 0.02 (= the absolute saturation ceiling; a relative reading below it would contradict the absolute one)", "baselineSaturation": 0.0, "relLuminanceChange": 0.0, "absSaturationDelta": 0.004, "absChromaDelta": 0.5, "fired": false, "reasons": []}

results.test: the absolute branch still FIRES on a large absolute change
results.detail: {"coding": "absolute", "codingChosenBy": "baseline interior saturation 0.00000 < 0.02 (= the absolute saturation ceiling; a relative reading below it would contradict the absolute one)", "baselineSaturation": 0.0, "relLuminanceChange": 0.0, "absSaturationDelta": 0.09, "absChromaDelta": 9.0, "fired": true, "reasons": ["interior saturation moved 0.0900 > 0.02", "interior chroma moved 9.000 > 2.0"]}

results.test: a well-supported baseline takes the RELATIVE branch and fires at 50%
results.detail: {"coding": "relative", "codingChosenBy": "baseline interior saturation 0.60000 >= 0.02 (= the absolute saturation ceiling; a relative reading below it would contradict the absolute one)", "baselineSaturation": 0.6, "relLuminanceChange": 0.0, "relSaturationChange": 0.5, "fired": true, "reasons": ["interior saturation moved 50.0% > 12%"]}

results.test: the branch floor equals the absolute ceiling, so the two codings cannot contradict each other
the branch depends on the BASELINE only, not on the candidate
a NON-MONOTONIC pointer path FAILS
results.detail: {"targetNxPath": [0.2, 0.5, 0.8], "candidateNxPath": [0.2, 0.9, 0.3], "adjacentJumps": [0.7, 0.6], "targetDirection": 1, "targetRange": 0.6, "candidateRange": 0.7, "branch": "tracking-reference", "branchChosenBy": "target path range 0.6000 >= 0.05", "fired": true, "reasons": ["adjacent jump 0.7000 > 0.4", "candidate path not monotonic in the target direction"]}

results.test: a path monotonic in the target's direction PASSES
a path moving the WRONG way FAILS
an unmeasurable state FAILS rather than passing quietly
zero_errors accepts an all-zero dict
zero_errors ignores a sibling bool verdict flag rather than counting it
zero_errors rejects a real non-zero count
a BOOL passed as an error record fails fast
a MISSING error record fails fast
a dict with no numeric counts fails fast
an unusable type fails fast
require_number rejects a bool masquerading as a count
require_number rejects a missing key
require_number accepts a real number
a large, stable, low-interaction factor is ELIGIBLE
a factor explaining under 40% is NOT eligible
a factor dominated by interaction is NOT eligible
a factor that flips sign across media is NOT eligible
a factor not sign-stable across viewports is NOT eligible
a factor that is largest on only half the media is NOT eligible
